Udaan Her Rise · Empower · Lead
From learning to earning.
A voice-first AI mentor for women with limited literacy in rural India.
Abstract

Udaan Her is a voice-first AI mentor for low-literacy women in rural India. In her own language it finds what she already knows, teaches a vocational skill in short spoken lessons grounded in real tutorials, checks understanding by conversation, re-teaches where she’s stuck, and ends every skill in earning — make → price → sell. No reading, no typing.

Problem Statement

India’s female labour-force participation hit 41.7% (2023-24) — but mostly rural, unpaid and self-employed, with ~77% of rural working women in agriculture. Skilling that could change this assumes literacy, menus and classrooms — excluding the women who need it most. Existing voice tools recruit by phone; none assess, teach, and connect skill to income.

Objectives
  • Zero literacy barrier — voice only, never read or type
  • Assess first — never re-teach what she already knows
  • Grounded teaching — from real tutorials, not hallucinated curricula
  • Learning → earning — every skill ends in make, price, sell
  • Any skill — generalized engine; skills are data, not code
  • Remembers her — persistent profile & per-concept mastery
Methodology & Results

Methodology — a two-speed design

A two-speed design. A slow lane sources real tutorials, transcribes and translates them via Sarvam, and distills grounded lessons offline. A fast lane (a live LangGraph mentor) runs the loop per turn: assess → path over only her gaps → teach → conversational viva → re-teach → earn. Video or diagram aids support, never gate, the lesson.

Results MVP target

MVP target: a woman completes a full loop by voice — profile saved, lesson taught with visuals, viva grading each concept strong / shaky, a wrong answer triggering a different re-teach, progress matching the database — at median turn latency ≤ 5s.

Process
Kiosk / Demo
The agent drives the screen — she only ever speaks or taps.
Sustainability Model

How does it sustain? (she never pays)

The learner is the beneficiary, not the customer. Revenue comes from the institutions already funded to skill her.
